# Third-party setup

From the repository root:

```bash
./third_party/install-kernels.sh
./third_party/prep-macro.sh
```

Both scripts use `third_party/sources/` by default and reuse existing sources. The kernel script builds and installs `6.3.0-colloid-alto`, `5.15.19-htmm`, and `5.15.145-mttm`; the two 5.15 kernels require rootless Podman.

Kernel setup can also be run in separate stages:

```bash
./third_party/install-kernels.sh --prepare-sources [kernel] [source-dir]
./third_party/install-kernels.sh --build [kernel] [source-dir]
./third_party/install-kernels.sh --install [kernel] [source-dir]
```

`--prepare-sources` downloads the sources, applies the patches, and configures the kernels. `--build` creates the Debian packages, and `--install` installs packages created by the build step. Packages for the 5.15 kernels are stored under `third_party/sources/packages/<kernel-release>/`.

`prep-macro.sh [source-dir]` builds llama-bench, FAISS, DRAMHiT, and VHT, downloads the Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M model and missing FAISS resources, and prints the executable and model paths. It installs Intel oneAPI through APT if needed; set `ONEAPI_SETVARS` for a nonstandard installation.

Copy `configs/site.example.conf` to `configs/site.conf` and set the printed paths there. Supply the licensed SPEC CPU 2017 installation separately. The kernel sources, application binaries, and model weights are not included in this repository.

## FAISS index and query files

Suppose `faiss_root` is set to the absolute path of the FAISS repo, such as `$(pwd)/third_party/sources/faiss`.

To generate the `SIFT100M_IVF128,PQ32_populated.index` file, download and decompress the [BIGANN learning vectors](ftp://ftp.irisa.fr/local/texmex/corpus/bigann_learn.bvecs.gz) into `${faiss_root}/bigann/`:

```bash
mkdir -p "${faiss_root}/bigann"
curl -L ftp://ftp.irisa.fr/local/texmex/corpus/bigann_learn.bvecs.gz \
    -o "${faiss_root}/bigann/bigann_learn.bvecs.gz"
gzip -dk "${faiss_root}/bigann/bigann_learn.bvecs.gz"
```

The FAISS benchmark script also reads `bigann_base.bvecs`, `bigann_query.bvecs`, and `bigann/gnd/idx_100M.ivecs` relative to `${faiss_root}`. Obtain the [BIGANN base vectors](ftp://ftp.irisa.fr/local/texmex/corpus/bigann_base.bvecs.gz), [queries](ftp://ftp.irisa.fr/local/texmex/corpus/bigann_query.bvecs.gz), and [ground truth](ftp://ftp.irisa.fr/local/texmex/corpus/bigann_gnd.tar.gz), then extract them to the corresponding paths. Once these files are present and the Python `faiss` module and NumPy are available, run:

```bash
cd "${faiss_root}"
python "./benchs/bench_polysemous_1bn.py" SIFT100M 'IVF128,PQ32'
```

The populated index is written to `/tmp/bench_polysemous/SIFT100M_IVF128,PQ32_populated.index`. Set `FAISS_INDEX` in `configs/site.conf` to that file or copy it to the path configured there.

The `bigann_50w_queries.bvecs` workload file was generated by randomly sampling 500,000 vectors without replacement from the first 10 million vectors in `bigann_base.bvecs`. To generate an equivalent query file, run:

```bash
mkdir -p third_party/resources
python3 - "${faiss_root}/bigann/bigann_base.bvecs" \
    third_party/resources/bigann_50w_queries.bvecs <<'PY'
import sys
import numpy as np

source = np.memmap(sys.argv[1], dtype=np.uint8, mode="r")
dimension = source[:4].view(np.int32)[0]
vectors = source.reshape(-1, dimension + 4)[:10_000_000, 4:]
indices = np.random.choice(vectors.shape[0], size=500_000, replace=False)
queries = vectors[indices]

records = np.empty((queries.shape[0], dimension + 4), dtype=np.uint8)
records[:, :4] = np.array([dimension], dtype=np.int32).view(np.uint8)
records[:, 4:] = queries
records.tofile(sys.argv[2])
PY
```

Because the sampling was not seeded, use the prepared file for an exact reproduction. Set `FAISS_QUERIES` in `configs/site.conf` to the generated or prepared file. When `FAISS_INDEX` or `FAISS_QUERIES` is missing, `prep-macro.sh` downloads the corresponding prepared file from the public [Spectra resources release](https://github.com/zelenyaz/spectra/releases/tag/resources-v1), verifies its SHA-256, and restores it at the configured path. The example config places both files under `third_party/resources/`. Existing nonempty files are left in place. The index is downloaded as three compressed parts; interrupted downloads can resume from `third_party/resources/.release-cache/`.
